// @autogenerated
Uid* (string)::
Unique identifier of the rule.
Name* (string)::
Name shown in the notices.
Trigger* (ObservedAlertRuleTriggerOptions)::
What fires the rule: new-issue, regression, error-rate (errors per minute above threshold during window-minutes), source-silent (no event during window-minutes), collector-dropping (the queue discards events), slo-burn (an objective spends its error budget too fast), probe-down (a probe fails its checks), tls-expiring (the certificate of a probe expires soon) or anomaly (traffic, errors or latency of an origin out of what is usual for that hour).Los posibles valores que toma el campo son:
 * new-issue
 * regression
 * error-rate
 * source-silent
 * collector-dropping
 * slo-burn
 * probe-down
 * tls-expiring
 * anomaly

Origin (xref:#entidad-observed-source[ObservedSource])::
Origin the rule watches; empty for every origin.
Min level* (ObservedAlertRuleMinLevelOptions)::
For new-issue and regression: minimum level of the issue.Los posibles valores que toma el campo son:
 * error
 * fatal

Threshold* (integer)::
For error-rate: errors per minute (average of the window) that fire the rule.
Window minutes* (integer)::
For error-rate and source-silent: minutes of the evaluation window.
Channel* (ObservedAlertRuleChannelOptions)::
Where the notice goes: log (a warning in the log of the application), webhook (POST JSON, compatible with Slack and Teams) or email (needs multitenant-notification).Los posibles valores que toma el campo son:
 * log
 * webhook
 * email

Target (string)::
Comma-separated emails, or the URL of the webhook.
Cooldown minutes* (integer)::
Minimum minutes between two notices of the same rule and problem.
Muted until (datetime)::
The rule does not notify until this moment (maintenance windows); the alerts are still recorded.
Enabled* (boolean)::
A disabled rule is not evaluated.
Version (integer)::
Campo con el número de version de observed alert rule para controlar bloqueos optimistas
